cases.user_input: What is a frequent problem encountered in brain computed tomography image classification when using machine learning and deep learning algorithms?
cases.response: A frequent problem is class imbalance: brain CT datasets may have far fewer examples of the clinically important classes (e.g., hemorrhagic stroke or specific hemorrhage subtypes) than normal/majority classes, which can bias machine learning and deep learning classifiers. Hossain et al., for example, used data-augmentation methods to address class imbalance problems when classifying stroke in CT images [S1]. Another related issue is limited training data in medical imaging, which is why transfer learning—such as using an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18—is commonly employed [S7].
